whatItIs.title: What a sequence is, and what it is not
whatItIs.sequenceText: a cadence of planned touches around one contact: first message, follow-up, proof, close-loop.
whatItIs.automationText: an action triggered by a rule or an event, without you being there.
whatItIs.journeyText: where a deal stands in your process, stage by stage.

channels.title: What the engine can actually do, per channel
channels.emailReady: Your mailbox is connected. The message is PREPARED and dated — you send it, or delegate sending through a bounded mandate.
channels.emailMissing: No mailbox connected. Messages are still prepared, and can be copied.
channels.reminderWhat: A dated reminder inside {{brand}}, for what you do yourself — a call, a message on a network.
channels.taskWhat: A dated task, for what happens before writing — check a signal, align with the delivery team.
channels.nothingAuto: Nothing goes out on its own: without a mandate, every email waits for your action. A mandate is your explicit, bounded, revocable action; private messages on a network and calls are never sent automatically.
channels.onlyThree: The engine knows these three step kinds and no others. A channel that is not listed here is not “coming soon”: it does not exist.

prospection_3_touches.when: The general case: a known contact, a first message, a reminder, a follow-up.
prospection_3_touches.outcome: Get a first answer, even a no.

cold_linkedin.when: Cold account, over a network: no pressure before they accept. Following up on someone who has not accepted yet is being ignored twice.

cold_email.when: Cold account, by email: each touch carries DIFFERENT information. Repeating the same message three times is not a cadence.
cold_email.outcome: Land a conversation, or a clear answer that closes the door.

fresh_signal.when: A very fresh signal: move fast, but check the signal first — a misread signal burns the account for six months.
fresh_signal.outcome: Be the first to raise it, with the right angle.

profile_push.when: An available profile to put forward: availability and proof, never a generic CV. The window is short.
profile_push.outcome: Get a date to present the profile.

existing_client.when: An active client: internal alignment comes BEFORE the follow-up. Writing without knowing what the delivery team is doing is the surest way to contradict yourself.

single_message.when: A single message is enough: a precise question, an answer to give — no cadence to build for a contact you already know.
single_message.outcome: Get an answer to ONE question, without committing to a follow-up.

call_session.when: A call session: phone first, not a written message waiting for a reply — useful when the conversation is worth more than text.
call_session.outcome: Get a live exchange, or a callback time.

light_sequence.when: A light cadence: two touches, widely spaced — so as not to pressure a contact you don't want to rush.
light_sequence.outcome: Stay visible without seeming to insist.

nurturing.when: A relationship to NURTURE, not convert right away: the pace is monthly, never an insistent follow-up.
nurturing.outcome: Stay the person they think of the day the need appears.

post_meeting_followup.when: Right after a meeting: the recap fixes what was said before it fades, then two tight follow-ups while the meeting is still fresh.
post_meeting_followup.outcome: Move the decision forward while the meeting is still top of mind.

referred_contact.when: A referral you received: the person already knows why you are reaching out, but the source is only named if they authorized it.
referred_contact.outcome: Turn the referral into a real exchange.

dormant_connection.when: An existing link gone quiet: acknowledge the time passed, give a real reason to reconnect, without false closeness.
dormant_connection.outcome: Reopen a link that had gone cold.

esn_partner.when: An ESN partner — a referral source or subcontracting relationship: a business relationship between two companies, not a prospect to convert.
esn_partner.outcome: Build a lasting collaboration, kept up over time.

purpose.cold_email.0: First contact — the problem you know how to solve
purpose.cold_email.1: Value follow-up — something they did not know
purpose.cold_email.2: Social proof — a comparable case, with numbers
purpose.cold_email.3: Close-loop — say this is the last one
purpose.fresh_signal.0: Check the signal — a misread signal burns the account for six months

purpose.fresh_signal.3: Close-loop — close before the signal goes cold

purpose.existing_client.0: Sync with the delivery team — know before you write
purpose.existing_client.1: Adjacent proposal — start from what already runs

purpose.single_message.0: Single message — the whole question, no follow-up planned
purpose.call_session.0: Call — the conversation is worth more than text here

purpose.post_meeting_followup.2: Close-loop — get a decision or a clear reason to wait

mandates.title: Sends under a signed mandate
mandates.intro: Nothing goes out on its own without your signature. Each use has its own mandate: you sign it, it is bounded (duration, volume, time window, per your plan), revocable at any time, renewable by signing again, and it stops at the first reply. Opt-outs, exclusions and erasures are checked again before every send.
mandates.noMailbox: Without a connected mailbox, no mandate can be signed: nothing could be sent or tracked.

status.none: No mandate: every message waits for your approval

mandates.pausedHint: Nothing is sent while the mandate is paused. Resume whenever you like: no need to sign it again.

dialog.bounds: {{days}} days · at most {{max}} sends · between {{start}}:00 and {{end}}:00
dialog.checkbox: I sign this mandate and I know I can revoke it at any time.

delegation.title: Sending delegation
delegation.intro: Only email can be delegated: a mandate you approve, limited to contacts, a time window, a duration and a volume. It stops at the first reply and can be revoked at any time. Private messages on a network and calls remain tasks for you.
delegation.noMailbox: Without a connected mailbox, no delegation is possible: nothing could go out or be tracked.
delegation.manualOnly: No delegation: every email waits for your approval before it goes out.

hiring_signal.0: Name the exact role and a close achievement. One question only.
hiring_signal.1: No note: the name and title are enough, the note comes later.
hiring_signal.2: Present a typical profile (stack, seniority), never a full CV.
hiring_signal.3: Prepare 3 points: the role, the profile, the opening question.
hiring_signal.4: Soft close: “I will stop following up, the door stays open”.

new_cio.0: Congratulate without selling: one sentence about the new role.
new_cio.1: Offer a review of the current situation, not a demo. They keep control.
new_cio.2: Tell a comparable client’s story, with numbers if you have them.
new_cio.3: Call with a single opening question about their scope.
new_cio.4: Close: say you remain available once their priorities are set.

tender.0: Ask one precise framing question (scope, budget, timeline) rather than introducing yourself.
tender.1: Call to get the answer to your question, not to pitch.
tender.2: Attach two references close to the need, not your whole showcase.
tender.3: Open the tender and note the deadline: it is your real due date.

win_back.0: Recall the past collaboration, then ONE new thing useful to them.
win_back.1: Light tone: you already know each other, no introduction.
win_back.2: Ask for news before talking about an offer.
win_back.3: Propose 15 minutes, never a long meeting.

after_meeting.0: Summarize what was said and the next steps, with dates.
after_meeting.1: Send the promised resource without adding a new ask.
after_meeting.2: Call to remove the last doubt, not to chase.
after_meeting.3: Ask where the decision stands and what is missing to move on.

bench_consultant.0: Anonymized profile: seniority, stack, availability. No name.
bench_consultant.1: Invite without a note; the reason for your message is in the email.
bench_consultant.2: Call early: an available profile does not stay available.
bench_consultant.3: Offer two alternative profiles to widen the way in.
bench_consultant.4: Say you are releasing the profile: it is honest and prompts an answer.

regie_to_forfait.0: A concrete case of a fixed-price project delivered for a close client.
regie_to_forfait.1: A short message pointing to the case, no pitch.
regie_to_forfait.2: Ask about their NEXT project rather than the current contract.
regie_to_forfait.3: Call with the case in hand and offer to frame a scope together.

warm_contact.0: Invite with a reminder of where and when you met.
warm_contact.1: An email that picks up one precise point from your conversation.
warm_contact.2: Call to propose a short, concrete next step.

0.subject: Your scope at {{companyName}}
0.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I’m trying to understand who owns this topic at {{companyName}}. Is it within your scope, or would you point me to someone else on the team?

Best regards,
{{signature}}

1.subject: Re: Your scope at {{companyName}}
1.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

Following up on my earlier message. Is there anything I should clarify so that you can answer?

Best regards,
{{signature}}

2.subject: Last message on this topic
2.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I don’t want to keep chasing you, so I’ll pause this follow-up. Just tell me if another time suits you better.

Best regards,
{{signature}}

0.subject: A topic that could help at {{companyName}}
0.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

We have supported teams close to yours on a related topic. If it could matter to {{companyName}}, I can tell you a few words about it.

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

1.subject: Re: A topic that could help
1.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

Picking up my previous message: would you like me to send a concrete example, no strings attached?

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

2.subject: To wrap up
2.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

Without a reply I’ll assume this isn’t a priority. I remain available if that changes.

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

0.subject: Following our conversation
0.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

Thank you for your time. So that nothing gets lost, here is what I took from our meeting and the next step I suggest.

Best regards,
{{signature}}

1.subject: Re: Following our conversation
1.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I’m checking whether the proposed next step suits you, or whether you’d rather adjust it.

Best regards,
{{signature}}

2.subject: Decision point
2.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

Could we set a short call to settle the next step? I’ll fit your calendar.

Best regards,
{{signature}}

0.subject: A profile for your need at {{companyName}}
0.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I’m writing about your need. An available profile matches what you are looking for; I can present it in a few lines.

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

1.subject: Re: A profile for your need
1.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I’m coming back to the profile I mentioned. Shall I send its presentation, or has the need changed?

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

2.subject: Profile still available
2.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

This profile stays available for a few more days. Let me know if you want to move forward; otherwise I’ll close this follow-up.

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

0.subject: A check-in after the start
0.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

A few weeks after the start, I wanted to make sure all is well: onboarding, access, scope. Is there anything to adjust?

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

1.body:
Hello {{firstName}},

I’m checking whether you had time to think it over. Three minutes are enough.

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

To plan ahead without assuming anything, could we talk about your priorities for the coming months?

Kind regards,
{{signature}}

Could you validate the activity report concerned? I’m available if anything needs clarifying.

{{signature}}

I’m following up on the report awaiting your validation.

web.title: A template from a web page
web.lead: {{copilot}} reads the page (your offer, a published case study) and proposes a three-step outline. What is not on the page stays as a variable to fill in.
